title: The Jack Unterweger Murders
evidence: Unterweger was convicted of a murder in Austria in 1976
He was released from prison after being regarded as rehabilitated
Eleven additional murders were attributed to him in Austria, the United States, and Czechoslovakia
Forensic psychiatric examination identified severe personality pathology
modus_operandi: Unterweger targeted women, particularly prostitutes, establishing contact before attacking them. Victims were strangled, and the murders involved sexual and sadistic elements.
personality_disorder: A forensic psychiatric examination identified numerous features of malignant narcissism and antisocial personality pathology, together with pronounced sadistic characteristics.
summary: Austrian serial killer and convicted murderer who became a celebrated writer while imprisoned and was released early after being regarded as rehabilitated. Within months of his release, he committed additional murders across Europe and the United States. He was later convicted of 11 murders.
